design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (root rx_ext_otc_catalog_order). Revised in rework round 2.

1. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5, 4, 6, 4]. Assignment: forfeiture 4, load 6, receipt posting 5, catalog order 4 (multiset {4,4,5,6} = draw).

2. Scope snapshot. First task; claims the four over-the-counter policies (rx_ext_otc_quarter_forfeit, rx_ext_otc_quarter_load, rx_ext_otc_receipt_posting, rx_ext_otc_catalog_order) and tools forfeit_otc_quarter_0e0fa26e, load_otc_quarter_30ec28e6, post_otc_receipt_a5c098d1, place_otc_catalog_order_ca6274ae. Task 1 holds the dispensing-days writes on rx_fills. rx_exceptions carries no numeric field, so exception requests and lock-in changes are not scored problems.

3. Why a good test. The member asks only for a catalog order with as much allowance as allowed. The order rule waits on every retail receipt transmitted for the current quarter (defined as the calendar quarter containing today) carrying a posting date; RCPT-0806-44719 is unposted. The posting rule waits on the load of the receipt's quarter; 2026-Q3 has none. The load rule waits on a forfeiture entry for the latest quarter loaded; 2026-Q2 has none. The agent works the chain forward on each handling-time world.

4. Problem-tree card. Chain forfeit -> load -> posting -> order (owner=user root), three state-form value_input edges: order<-posting (gate order_balance), posting<-load (gate posting_balance, negated sentence 'is not posted until'), load<-forfeit (gate closeout_credit). Opening evidence: receipt row posted_date ''; loads only 2026-Q1/Q2; forfeiture only 2026-Q1. Skip runs: skip posting -> order 46.05; skip load -> posting limited to 6.00; skip forfeiture -> load 73.75. Each state is brought about by exactly one write of the difficulty. user_scenario names no prerequisite; no tool validates one.

5. Factor card (tier / baseline figure from the sens run on each handling-time world):
 forfeiture (baseline 6.22): carryover_share 0.5 [plan: Pregnancy Care + 5 paid preventive claims] /6.22; carryover_usage 1 [43.78/50] /6.22; carryover_ceiling 6.00 [6 months] /6.22; carryover_base method = full load [one online order, 6 months] /3.11. Declared overwrite of the base rollover sentence.
 load (baseline 50.00): pregnancy supply 10 /65.75; income supplement 5 /70.75; shipping credit 2.50 /73.25; late-load accrual method 2.25 /73.50; care program 4 /71.75; closeout 2 /73.75.
 receipt charge (baseline 79.74): eligible share 1.00 /54.83; price adjustment 0.02 [two posted retail receipts in six months] /62.17; large-receipt split method /65.99; care co-funding 0.20 /76.16; low-income relief 0.05 /64.13.
 catalog order (baseline 10.88): withheld_carryover parameter 1 [posted 2026-Q3 receipt, two orders open] /6.50; order_share 0.6 [two open, forfeited-quarter usage 0.8756] /4.83; keep_back_count_window method = rolling two whole months [Maternity allows 2 remote orders, 2026-Q2 had an online order: 2026-06-28 and 2026-08-19 receipts] against the calendar-quarter count /5.90; shipping_fee 0 /0.00.
 Near-misses: preventive claim 2026-02-11 (more than six whole months back), 2026-07-22 denied, retail receipt 2026-02-16 (more than six whole months back), RCPT-0628-19027 (inside the two-month window, outside the one-month window and outside 2026-Q3), the unposted receipt itself.

6. Base-invariant card. rx_otc_allowance gate otc_on_open_coverage (coverage active) for load, posting and order, bound through rx_coverage_id; forfeiture has no structured gate (policy_scope). No time gate.

7. Business-object card. Forfeiture: 2026-Q2 rows (o4, o5, o6, o8). Posting: the largest (only) unposted retail receipt o7. Order: new mail catalog row tagged 2026-Q3.

8. Persona unchanged: catalog-order goal only, passive consent to account work, Medicaid ID + 1996-11-03, places the order herself, reads back the order number.

9. Standard solution: find_customers -> verify -> find_rx_coverages -> find_rx_otc_ledger -> find_plan_memberships -> find_plan_claims -> find_care_enrollments -> forfeit 2026-Q2 -> load 2026-Q3 -> post RCPT-0806-44719 -> member places catalog order.

10. Verification: check_compute, replay, solvability, extended, task tools, grounding, scope all OK after round 2; figures above from scratch sens.py.

11. Revision log. Round 1: posting tool gained rx_coverage_id; persona DOB verbatim. Round 2 (audit CG-F1/CG-F2): catalog order factors rebuilt (reachable order-share tiers; withheld carry-over as a parameter with non-degenerate conditions; keep-back counting window as the method); 'current quarter' defined as the calendar quarter; keep-back standard count uses posted receipts without an invented window; carry-over floor stated; register total = largest unposted receipt; world gained retail receipt RCPT-0628-19027 (2026-Q2), so the opening balance, the forfeiture and the order were recomputed; rationale wording on the 2026-02-11 claim corrected to 'more than six whole months back'.
Round 3 (audit R2-T1): the receipt-posting rule now defines 'the last six whole months' (fewer than six whole calendar months from the date to today, a month whole once today's day of the month reaches the date's day) and uses that wording in every window sentence; the Q1 retail receipt was moved to 2026-02-16 so no posted receipt sits on the six-month anniversary. The price-adjustment tier therefore has one reading (two posted receipts). The vacation baseline sentence now states the one-day floor the compute applies.
user_scenario:
You are Seraphina Kowalczyk-Adeyemi, twenty-nine, about seven months pregnant, calling Prairie Ridge member services from your kitchen in Lincoln on a Wednesday morning. You are friendly, a little tired, and you like to get things done in one call. You have your member ID card in front of you.

You open by saying you would like to order from the over-the-counter catalog: you have been eyeing the prenatal comfort items and a few baby-prep things, and you want to put as much of your over-the-counter allowance toward a catalog order as the plan will let you use on it. You want the order placed today, and you are happy to place it yourself if they set it up for you. Anything above what the allowance covers you will handle on your own; you are not asking for anything else today.

When they ask who you are, you give your Medicaid ID, PR30417726, and your date of birth, which you read off as 1996-11-03. Only if they ask for more, your phone number is 4025530627, your ZIP code is 68505 and the last four of your Social Security number are 3462. You do not know any account or reference numbers beyond your Medicaid ID.

You do not know how the allowance is calculated and you do not ask about the details; you do not bring up your balance, earlier purchases or anything else on your pharmacy account. If the representative explains that something has to be taken care of on the account before the order can be worked out, you say that is fine and they can go ahead and do whatever needs doing on their side. If they ask whether you have anything else going on, you say it is just the catalog order. When they tell you the order is ready for you to place and hand it over to you, you place it exactly as they set it up, and once it goes through you read back the order number it gives you. If they tell you how much of the allowance is going on the order, you accept it; you do not argue about the figure. After the order number comes back, you thank them and end the call.

The ledger's latest load (posted 2026-04-01) is tagged 2026-Q2. Uniqueness: no 2026-Q3 load exists yet and 2026-Q1 already carries its forfeiture (3.85 posted 2026-03-31), so no other quarter qualifies.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain forfeit -> load -> receipt posting -> catalog order, and each prerequisite sentence fixes one link: 'The quarter load is fixed only after the ledger carries a forfeiture entry for the latest quarter loaded before it.', 'A transmitted retail receipt is not posted until the ledger carries the load of the benefit quarter the receipt is tagged to.', 'The allowance applied to a catalog order is fixed only after every retail receipt transmitted for the current quarter carries a posting date.' No two writes are parallel, so there is exactly one topological order.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the receipt posting leaves otc_balance at 81.75 and no posted 2026-Q3 retail receipt: nothing of the carry-over is withheld, the two-month window counts one receipt (keep-back 5.00), and the order allowance becomes 46.05 instead of the gold figure; the receipt row also keeps an empty posted_date.
Skipping the load leaves the posting balance at 6.00, so the receipt allowance charge is limited to 6.00 instead of the gold figure, and no 2026-Q3 load row exists.
Skipping the forfeiture leaves 2026-Q2 with no forfeiture entry, so the closeout credit is 0 and the load is 73.75 instead of the gold figure; otc_balance also stays higher by the forfeited amount.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for a catalog order with as much allowance as the plan lets her use. It never mentions the balance, a quarter's forfeiture, a missing load, a register receipt or posting, and it contains no hint that something must be settled first; the only line about prior work is the passive 'If the representative explains that something has to be taken care of on the account before the order can be worked out, you say that is fine'.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: In task_tools.py, place_otc_catalog_order_ca6274ae, post_otc_receipt_a5c098d1 and load_otc_quarter_30ec28e6 each perform one ctx.create/ctx.update on rx_otc_ledger plus the otc_balance update on rx_coverages and return a receipt; none reads the ledger for missing forfeitures, loads or unposted receipts, none refuses, and none returns an error when a prerequisite is unresolved.
